Skyrmion Fractional Chern Insulator: An Intrinsically Multiband Route to Fractionalization in Rhombohedral Graphene

Julian May-Mann,1, ∗Tixuan Tan (谈体轩),1, ∗Patrick J. Ledwith,2 Zhengyan Darius Shi (石铮岩),1 and Trithep Devakul1, †

1Department of Physics, Stanford University, Stanford, CA 94305, USA 2Department of Physics, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA 02139, USA (Dated: August 17, 2026)

We propose an unconventional microscopic origin for the fractional quantum anomalous Hall (FQAH) effect in rhombohedral graphene moir´e superlattices: skyrmion fractionalization. We view the state at filling ν < 1 as a metal of skyrmion vacancies, charge +e objects formed by removing layer-pseudospin skyrmions from the interaction-generated skyrmion lattice Chern insulator at ν = 1. These vacancies are intrinsically multiband degrees of freedom, absent in single Chern band-projected studies. Building on a recently proposed ideal limit, we first develop an effective field theory showing that skyrmion vacancies can themselves fractionalize, thereby inducing charge fractionalization. Focusing on ν = 2

3, we then construct explicit variational trial wavefunctions for the resulting skyrmion fractional Chern insulator and provide numerical evidence, together with general arguments, showing that this process is energetically favored. Our results establish a realistic route to the FQAH that does not rely on a partially filled Chern band, but instead arises from fractionalization of collective pseudospin textures.

## INTRODUCTION

Electron fractionalization, as exemplified by the fractional quantum Hall (FQH) effect, is a hallmark of strongly correlated topological quantum matter. The recent experimental observations of its zero magnetic field counterpart, the fractional quantum anomalous Hall (FQAH) effect [1, 2], in twisted MoTe2 [3–6] and rhombohedral N-layer graphene (RNG) on hBN [7–14], have renewed interest in these phases, particularly in the novel aspects of their realization at zero field and their microscopic origin. At its core, the conventional picture for the FQAH closely parallels the FQH effect: strongly interacting electrons partially fill a C = 1 band and form a fractional Chern insulator (FCI) [15–22]. In tMoTe2 [23–25] (and finite-field FCIs [26–34]), an isolated C = 1 band makes this picture natural [35–39], and band-projected exact diagonalization (ED) at fractional moir´e filling factors 0 < ν < 1 yields FCIs. R5G/hBN is less straightforward because its single-particle spectrum lacks a well-isolated Chern band (Fig 1A shows the unfolded R5G conduction band). Instead, Hartree-Fock (HF) theory produces an interaction-generated C = 1 band at filling ν = 1 in the folded moir´e Brillouin zone [40–53] (Fig 1B.i.), which is then used as a basis for band-projected ED at 0 < ν < 1 [40–43]. This HF-ED approach works even in the moir´e-less limit, in which case they spontaneously break continuous translation symmetry realizing anomalous Hall crystals [54–71]. Despite the more roundabout

approach, these studies ultimately yield FCIs at partial filling of a single C = 1 band. However, this single-band projection in R5G/hBN is uncontrolled because the C = 1 band is itself interactiongenerated. Indeed, calculations that take into account multiple HF bands find that band mixing effects are strong [72–74]. The nature of these multiband effects is not fully understood: whether they merely dress a singleband FCI or reflect something intrinsic about its microscopic origin remains unclear. Here, we propose an unconventional, intrinsically multiband, route to fractionalization in rhombohedral graphene that we term the skyrmion FCI (SkFCI). Our starting point is the perspective [53] that the ν = 1 Chern insulator in R5G/hBN is an interaction-generated layerpseudospin skyrmion lattice (SkL), pinned by the moir´e potential, whose texture produces the emergent LLL-like C = 1 band (Fig 1B.i.). Upon reducing the filling below ν = 1, the conventional picture, assumed by HF-ED, dopes holes into this C = 1 band (Fig 1B.ii.). We instead consider skyrmion vacancies (SkVs), missing skyrmions in the lattice, as the lowest energy charge +e objects. Because the SkV involves a modification of the collective layer-pseudospin texture (Fig 1C), it is an intrinsically multiband and multielectron object (Fig 1B.iii.), absent in band-projected studies. This paints a very different picture for the metallic phase at ν < 1 as a metal of charge-carrying texture fluctuations. Motivated by this, we focus on ν = 2

3 and ask whether the parent state of the FCI could be a SkV metal rather than a hole metal. Do SkVs experience an effective magnetic field, and if so, can they fractionalize? Can such skyrmion fractionalization account for the observed σH = 2

3 FQAH, and is it energetically competitive? We answer all of these questions in the affirmative.

## CONCLUSIONS

In this work, we have established an intrinsically multiband route to the FQAH driven by skyrmion fractionalization and shown that such a scenario is energetically competitive in R5G/hBN. Our theory provides an explanation for the strong band mixing effects found in multiband studies and suggests a qualitatively unconventional microscopic origin of the observed phenomenology in R5G/hBN. More broadly, our results demonstrate that the FQAH need not originate from a partially filled Chern band, but can instead emerge from fractionalization of collective pseudospin textures.
